plan_summary: Give the terminal failure-reason vocabulary an explicit severity split, sourced from the classification execution-report.js already computes. Four files change, all inside policy.allowed_paths. (1) execution-report.js: add EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH to NO_RETRY_REASONS and QUARANTINE_REASONS (the new distinct non-retriable reason for an integrity breach); add PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK to QUARANTINE_REASONS so the code stops contradicting the documented meaning it has carried since the reason was defined; add ONE severity predicate (failureReasonSeverity + the derived FAILURE_REASON_SEVERITY map) that decideLifecycle itself consults, so severity is computed once and never duplicated; export both; return an additional `classification` object from buildReport (module API only, NOT a new key in execution_report.json) and render the severity beside the failure reason in the markdown. (2) references/phase-gates.md: replace the prose 'Failure-reason classes' bullets with the canonical TERMINAL FAILURE-REASON table that defines every reason and states its severity in the same row, adds the EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH row, and makes ADVOCATE_DISSENT the MANDATORY reason for an upheld or unresolved dissent, overriding the blanket {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE default. (3) references/artifact-layout.md: state that run_manifest.failure_reason is a closed enum whose single definition is that table, and name EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH as the terminal reason at the two places the document already describes an integrity breach. (4) references/validator-inputs.md: document the exported classification as the orchestrator's sourcing channel for severity, and state that the emitted report schema is unchanged. Two deliberate boundaries, both forced by the policy: SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1.4.0 and no key is added to execution_report.json, because parity/execution-report-fixtures/run-tests.js pins schema_version to '1.4.0' and parity/ is a blocked path; and adws-pipeline/skill-manifest.json is NOT in allowed_paths, so the content digests it carries will go stale and Tier-1 local CI (scripts/local-ci/skill-manifest.mjs) will report the manifest as stale after this change — that must be surfaced to the operator as an out-of-scope follow-up, never silently regenerated by the builder.

file_change_proposal.description: Four additive edits, no change to the DECISIONS map, the exit-code function, or SCHEMA_VERSION (which stays '1.4.0'). (a) Add 'EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH' to both NO_RETRY_REASONS and QUARANTINE_REASONS, mirroring CREDENTIAL_FAILURE/MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT, so the breach the report already treats as 'the same class as MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT' has a terminal reason of its own instead of collapsing into {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE (criterion 3). (b) Add 'PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK' to QUARANTINE_REASONS: references/phase-gates.md has always defined it as quarantine-class on a second BLOCK while the code has it in neither set, i.e. scoring it RETRY — with the severity column now sourced from the code (criterion 4), that divergence would make the new table print a severity contradicting the reason's documented meaning, which constraint 2 forbids. This is a disclosed tie-break: the builder records it explicitly in implementation_notes and it changes no fixture (no parity fixture records that reason). (c) Add a single severity predicate — function failureReasonSeverity(reason) returning 'non-retriable' when QUARANTINE_REASONS or NO_RETRY_REASONS has the reason, 'retriable' for any other non-empty reason, and null for no reason — plus FAILURE_REASON_SEVERITY built programmatically from the union of the two sets (never a hand-written second table, which would drift). decideLifecycle's `failed` branch is refactored to consult that predicate while keeping its three existing decision_reason strings and the QUARANTINE-before-NO_RETRY ordering byte-identical, so severity is computed in exactly one place. Export failureReasonSeverity and FAILURE_REASON_SEVERITY from module.exports beside the existing NO_RETRY_REASONS/QUARANTINE_REASONS. (d) Return a third key from buildReport — classification: { failure_reason, severity, integrity_breach } — where integrity_breach is true when evidenceProblems is non-empty or any skill_verdict/superseded row carries a trace_mismatch. This is the structural signal that replaces reading 'EVIDENCE INTEGRITY:' out of a gate detail string, and it lives on the module's return value, NOT in the written execution_report.json, so no key is added to the emitted schema and no SCHEMA_VERSION bump is needed (parity pins '1.4.0' and parity/ is blocked). Finally, render the severity beside the reason in the markdown line '- **Failure reason:** X (non-retriable)' for the human reader; the markdown is only compared run-to-run for determinism, so this is parity-safe.

Replace the prose 'Failure-reason classes (port of phases.js reason sets)' bullet list (currently lines ~457-471) with the canonical 'Terminal failure-reason vocabulary' TABLE — the one place a terminal reason is defined — and update the two consensus sites that decide a dissent's terminal reason. The table has one row per reason (CREDENTIAL_FAILURE, OPERATOR_CANCEL, MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT, PLAN_COHERENCE_BELOW_THRESHOLD, ADVOCATE_DISSENT, EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH, PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK, PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED, STABILITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE) and columns: Reason | When it is recorded | Attempt policy (no-retry = stop spending attempts now / budgeted) | Terminal severity (non-retriable / retriable) | Report decision. The severity cell is stated in the SAME row the reason is defined in, which is criterion 1, and every cell is the value failureReasonSeverity() returns for that reason, which is criterion 4. Three further edits in the same file: (i) a normative sentence directly under the table that the severity column is a PROJECTION of execution-report.js's classification and must be re-read from it (`node -e "console.log(require('<skill>/scripts/execution-report.js').failureReasonSeverity('<REASON>'))"`), never re-derived by parsing a gate detail string or the decision_reason prose; (ii) a row-level rule making ADVOCATE_DISSENT the MANDATORY terminal reason for an unresolved dissent AND for resolution.action 'uphold' — it overrides SKILL.md step 4's default of {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE under that step's existing 'unless a more specific reason applies' clause — with the same statement added to the 'uphold' bullet of Consensus rule 5 (~line 371-373) and the unresolved-dissent sentence of Consensus rule 2 (~line 322), which today name ADVOCATE_DISSENT without saying it is what run_manifest.failure_reason must carry (criterion 2); (iii) an EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH row defining it as the terminal reason when the evidence tree itself is untrustworthy — a skill_trace.json whose rubric_result disagrees with its own output.rubric_result (latest or superseded), or an evidence file that exists and cannot be read/parsed — non-retriable, quarantine-class (criterion 3). A closing note keeps the attempt-level annotations CRITIC_FAIL_REPAIRED and ADVOCATE_DISSENT_REPAIRED explicitly OUT of the table and out of run_manifest.failure_reason, preserving their current meaning, and states that the vocabulary is a closed enum: a reason may be added here but never redefined and never replaced by free text.

Two edits that make the evidence schema point at the new single definition and name the new reason where the document already describes the breach. (a) In the run_manifest.json prose (the paragraph after the shape block, ~lines 60-68, next to the existing sentence about final_status) add: failure_reason is a CLOSED enum whose only definition — reason, when it is recorded, and its retriable/non-retriable severity — is the terminal failure-reason table in references/phase-gates.md; it is null while running and on a clean completion, never free text, and never a reason absent from that table. (b) In the SC-8/F-55 evidence-integrity paragraph (~lines 391-400), where the document already says a wrapper/validator disagreement 'quarantines the job — an evidence-integrity breach, the same class as MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT', name the terminal reason explicitly: the job terminates failed with EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH (non-retriable), not with {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE, and the same applies to an evidence file that exists and cannot be parsed (the SC-11/A1 unreadable-evidence path). This is what makes criterion 3 hold at the place a reader of the evidence schema actually looks, and it changes no file shape, no key, and no append-only rule.

Extend the execution-report.js rows in the two tables (the 'terminal state only' row ~line 94 and the outputs row ~line 113) with the sourcing channel criterion 4 requires: the script exports failureReasonSeverity(reason) and the derived FAILURE_REASON_SEVERITY map, and buildReport() returns a classification object { failure_reason, severity, integrity_breach } alongside { report, markdown }. State plainly that an orchestrator recording run_manifest.failure_reason takes the severity from that classification (or from the phase-gates table, which is its projection) and NEVER by parsing decision_reason or a gate's detail string, and that the emitted execution_report.json schema is unchanged — same keys, same decision/exit-code vocabulary (0/10/1/2, 3 = could not run), schema_version still 1.4.0 — so nothing about the report contract in these tables becomes stale.

criteria_map.criterion: The terminal failure reason vocabulary documents, for every reason, whether that reason is retriable or non-retriable, and the severity is stated in the same table the reason is defined in.
criteria_map.check_idea: Parse the terminal failure-reason table out of adws-pipeline/references/phase-gates.md with a script (split the markdown table rows) and assert: (a) a table exists; (b) it contains a row for every reason in the union of NO_RETRY_REASONS and QUARANTINE_REASONS as required from adws-pipeline/scripts/execution-report.js, plus {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE, STABILITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED and PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK; (c) EVERY row's severity cell is exactly 'retriable' or 'non-retriable' (no blank, no prose); (d) no reason token appears anywhere else in the file as a competing definition list. Falsifiability baseline: run the same script against the pre-change file obtained with `git show main:adws-pipeline/references/phase-gates.md` into the scratch root — it must go RED with 'no table found' (today the vocabulary is a prose bullet list), i.e. assertion-failed-runtime-present, and GREEN post-change.

criteria_map.criterion: An upheld advocate dissent terminates on a distinct non-retriable failure reason rather than on the blanket phase gate failure reason.
criteria_map.check_idea: Two-part check. (1) Doc binding: assert the phase-gates table's ADVOCATE_DISSENT row names 'uphold'/unresolved dissent as its trigger and that Consensus rule 5's uphold bullet states ADVOCATE_DISSENT is what run_manifest.failure_reason carries, overriding the {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE default. (2) Behaviour: `require()` execution-report.js and assert failureReasonSeverity('ADVOCATE_DISSENT') === 'non-retriable' while failureReasonSeverity('REVIEW_GATE_FAILURE') === 'retriable' — the two must not collapse; then build a synthetic job dir under the scratch root (run_manifest.json with final_status 'failed', failure_reason 'ADVOCATE_DISSENT') and assert the CLI exits 2 / decision QUARANTINE, and the same tree with 'REVIEW_GATE_FAILURE' exits 1 / RETRY. Falsifiability baseline: against `git show main:adws-pipeline/scripts/execution-report.js` the require-side assertion goes RED (failureReasonSeverity is not a function) and the doc assertion goes RED (no such row); the two CLI exits already hold pre-change and are the must-not-regress half, not the falsifiable half. No fixture is written anywhere under parity/.

criteria_map.criterion: An evidence integrity breach terminates on a distinct non-retriable failure reason rather than on the blanket phase gate failure reason.
criteria_map.check_idea: Assert EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH exists as a distinct reason and is non-retriable end to end: (a) require() the script and assert NO_RETRY_REASONS.has('EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH') && QUARANTINE_REASONS.has('EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH') && failureReasonSeverity('EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH') === 'non-retriable'; (b) build a synthetic job dir under the scratch root whose run_manifest.json records final_status 'failed' / failure_reason 'EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH' and assert the CLI exits 2 (QUARANTINE) with decision_reason naming it quarantine-class; (c) build a second synthetic job dir containing a skill_trace.json whose rubric_result disagrees with its own output.rubric_result and assert buildReport().classification.integrity_breach === true — the structural signal, not the gate detail string; (d) assert both reference docs name EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH at the integrity paragraphs. Falsifiability baseline: against the pre-change tree in the scratch root, (a) and (d) go RED and (b) exits 1/RETRY — the exact collapse this criterion removes.

criteria_map.criterion: The severity of a terminal failure reason is sourced from the classification execution-report.js already computes, not re-derived by an orchestrator parsing gate detail strings.
criteria_map.check_idea: Assert single-source-of-truth, not just presence: (a) require() the script and assert FAILURE_REASON_SEVERITY's key set equals exactly the union of NO_RETRY_REASONS and QUARANTINE_REASONS with every value 'non-retriable' — i.e. it is derived from those sets, so a reason added to a set cannot leave the map behind; (b) for every reason in that union plus three retriable controls (BUILD_GATE_FAILURE, TEST_GATE_FAILURE, STABILITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED), assert failureReasonSeverity(reason) agrees with the decision decideLifecycle returns for a 'failed' job carrying it (non-retriable iff QUARANTINE) — the predicate and the decision cannot disagree because decideLifecycle consults the predicate; (c) assert the phase-gates table's severity cells equal failureReasonSeverity() for every row, so the documentation is a projection and not a second table; (d) assert references/validator-inputs.md documents the exported channel and the prohibition on parsing decision_reason / gate detail; (e) regression: assert the emitted execution_report.json still has no severity key and schema_version === '1.4.0'. Falsifiability baseline: (a)-(d) all go RED against the pre-change tree (no export, no table); (e) is the must-not-regress guard and must be green on both sides. Plus the corpus-wide regression required by constraint 4: run `node parity/execution-report-fixtures/run-tests.js` and `node parity/cli-contract/run-tests.js` READ-ONLY (execute, never edit — parity/ is a blocked path) and require every fixture's decision, warn_flag and exit code to be unchanged.
